questions.question: A Customer Value Proposition (CVP) primarily answers which fundamental question?

options.text: How much does it cost to manufacture our product?
Why should a specific customer buy from us rather than from competitors?
How many employees do we need to hire?
When should we file for an IPO?

questions.explanation: A CVP clearly articulates the unique value delivered to a specific customer segment and why that customer should choose your offering over all available alternatives.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes 'customer segmentation'?

options.text: Dividing a market into distinct groups of buyers with different needs or behaviours
Selling the same product to all possible buyers without any targeting
A pricing strategy for premium products only
The process of hiring specialised sales teams

questions.explanation: Customer segmentation divides the market into groups sharing similar characteristics, needs, or behaviours, allowing targeted value creation and marketing.

questions.question: Which three components are central to a well-crafted Customer Value Proposition?

options.text: Price, place, and promotion
Target customer, jobs to be done (needs), and the unique benefit your solution provides
Revenue model, cost structure, and key partners
Technology stack, team size, and funding round

questions.explanation: A strong CVP identifies who the customer is, what job or need they have, and why your offering uniquely addresses that need better than alternatives.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of customer discovery in early-stage entrepreneurship?

options.text: To finalise the company logo and branding
To validate or invalidate assumptions about the customer and their problems before investing heavily in a solution
To negotiate contracts with suppliers
To determine the exact number of shares to issue

questions.explanation: Customer discovery involves talking to potential customers to test assumptions about the problem, solution, and business model before spending significant resources on development.

questions.question: Which statement about business models is most accurate?

options.text: A business model is a synonym for a financial projection spreadsheet
A business model describes how a company creates, delivers, and captures value
Business models are static and never need to change after launch
Only product companies need a defined business model

questions.explanation: A business model describes the logic of how an organisation creates value for customers, delivers that value, and in return captures economic value for itself.

questions.question: A standard CVP statement format typically includes which of the following elements?

options.text: Company registration number and tax ID
For [target customer], who [need or problem], our [product/service] provides [key benefit] unlike [alternative]
Monthly burn rate and runway
Number of GitHub commits and code coverage percentage

questions.explanation: A CVP format explicitly names the target customer, their need, the solution, the key benefit delivered, and differentiation from alternatives — making it clear and testable.

questions.question: Which segmentation basis divides customers by their lifestyle, attitudes, and values?

options.text: Geographic segmentation
Demographic segmentation
Psychographic segmentation
Behavioural segmentation

questions.explanation: Psychographic segmentation categorises customers by personality traits, values, interests, and lifestyles — going beyond demographics to understand motivations.

questions.question: Which of the following customer discovery practices is most likely to yield unreliable insights?

options.text: Conducting open-ended interviews without leading questions
Asking customers if they 'would buy' a hypothetical product
Observing customers in their natural environment
Analysing existing customer support complaints

questions.explanation: Asking hypothetical purchase-intent questions is notoriously unreliable — people say they would buy but often do not. Observational and behavioural data yield more reliable insights.
